faqs.q: What is JSON formatting?
faqs.a: JSON formatting is the process of adding proper indentation, line breaks, and spacing to JSON data to make it more readable. It doesn't change the data itself, just its visual presentation.

base64.name: Base64 编码/解码
base64.description: 将文本编码为 Base64 或将 Base64 解码回文本
base64.pageDescription: 将文本编码为 Base64 或将 Base64 字符串解码回纯文本。支持 UTF-8。免费使用，无需注册。
base64.seoContent: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data in an ASCII string format. It's commonly used for encoding data in URLs, emails, HTML, and APIs. You can also decode Base64 from the command line using openssl base64 decode: run 'echo <encoded> | openssl base64 -d'. This online Base64 encoder and decoder supports full UTF-8, handles Base64 padding (the trailing = characters), and works entirely in your browser. Whether you need to base64 encode a file, decode an API response, or convert data for URL-safe transport, this tool handles it instantly.

faqs.q: What is Base64 encoding?
faqs.a: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that converts binary data into ASCII characters. It's commonly used to transmit data safely over text-based protocols like HTTP and email.

faqs.q: Is Base64 encoding the same as encryption?
faqs.a: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. Anyone can decode Base64 data. It's meant for data transport, not security.

faqs.q: Does this tool support UTF-8?
faqs.a: Yes. This tool fully supports UTF-8 encoding and decoding, allowing you to work with international characters and emojis.

faqs.q: How do I use openssl to base64 decode on the command line?
faqs.a: Run 'echo <base64string> | openssl base64 -d' to decode. To encode, use 'echo -n "text" | openssl base64'. The openssl base64 command is available on macOS and Linux by default.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Base64 and Base64URL?
faqs.a: Standard Base64 uses + and / as special characters, while Base64URL replaces them with - and _ to be safe in URLs and filenames. Base64URL also omits padding (=) characters.

faqs.q: What is Base64 padding and why are there = signs?
faqs.a: Base64 encodes 3 bytes into 4 characters. When the input length isn't a multiple of 3, padding characters (=) are added to make the output length a multiple of 4. One = means 2 bytes were encoded in the last group, == means 1 byte.

faqs.q: Can I Base64 encode a file?
faqs.a: Yes. On the command line use 'base64 < file.bin > file.b64' or 'openssl base64 -in file.bin'. For images, use our Image Base64 Converter tool which supports drag-and-drop file encoding.

faqs.q: Is it safe to use Base64 in URLs?
faqs.a: Standard Base64 is not URL-safe because + and / have special meanings in URLs. Use Base64URL encoding instead, which replaces + with - and / with _ . Most programming languages have built-in Base64URL functions.

howToUseSteps: Enter your plain text in the top field to encode, or Base64 string in the bottom field to decode
Click 'Encode' to convert text to Base64, or 'Decode' to convert Base64 back to text
Copy the result with the copy button
useCases: Encoding images for embedding in HTML/CSS
Transmitting binary data in JSON APIs

url-encoder.seoContent: URL encoding replaces unsafe ASCII characters with a "%" followed by two hexadecimal digits. This is essential for passing special characters in URLs, query parameters, and form data. Use encodeURIComponent for query parameters and encodeURI for full URLs.

faqs.q: What is URL encoding?
faqs.a: URL encoding replaces unsafe ASCII characters with a '%' followed by two hex digits. This ensures special characters are safely transmitted in URLs.

faqs.q: What's the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faqs.a: encodeURI encodes a full URL but preserves characters like :, /, ?, &. encodeURIComponent encodes everything including those characters, making it suitable for query parameter values.

faqs.q: When should I URL encode?
faqs.a: Always URL encode when passing user input as query parameters, form data, or any URL component that may contain special characters like spaces, &, =, or #.

howToUseSteps: Enter text in the input field
Choose between URI Component or Full URI encoding mode
Click 'Encode' or 'Decode'
Copy the result
useCases: Handling special characters in API requests

hash-generator.name: 哈希生成器
hash-generator.description: 从文本生成 MD5、SHA-1、SHA-256、SHA-512 哈希
hash-generator.pageDescription: 从任意文本生成 SHA-1、SHA-256、SHA-384、SHA-512 哈希。均在浏览器中计算。免费使用，无需注册。
hash-generator.seoContent: Cryptographic hash functions generate a fixed-size hash value from input data. This online MD5 hash generator and SHA256 hash tool computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 hashes instantly in your browser. Hash functions are one-way: you cannot reverse a hash back to the original data. They're used for data integrity verification, password storage, digital signatures, file checksums, and deduplication. SHA-256 is recommended for security-sensitive applications, while MD5 remains useful for quick checksums despite being cryptographically broken.

faqs.q: What is a hash function?
faqs.a: A hash function takes input data and produces a fixed-size string of characters (hash). The same input always produces the same hash, but you cannot reverse a hash back to the original data.

faqs.q: Which hash algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: SHA-256 is recommended for most purposes. SHA-512 offers more security. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered weak for security but are still used for checksums.

faqs.q: Is my data safe?
faqs.a: Yes. All hash computation happens in your browser using the Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.q: What is the difference between MD5 and SHA-256?
faqs.a: MD5 produces a 128-bit (32 hex character) hash and is fast but cryptographically broken — collisions can be generated. SHA-256 produces a 256-bit (64 hex character) hash and is considered secure. Use SHA-256 for security, MD5 only for non-security checksums.

faqs.q: What is a hash collision?
faqs.a: A hash collision occurs when two different inputs produce the same hash output. MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision vulnerabilities. SHA-256 and SHA-512 have no known practical collisions and are considered collision-resistant.

faqs.q: What is a hash salt and why is it important?
faqs.a: A salt is random data added to the input before hashing, making each hash unique even for identical inputs. Salting prevents rainbow table attacks on password hashes. Always use a unique salt per password when storing hashed passwords.

faqs.q: When should I use bcrypt instead of SHA-256 for passwords?
faqs.a: Always use bcrypt (or Argon2, scrypt) for password hashing. SHA-256 is too fast, making brute-force attacks feasible. Bcrypt is intentionally slow and includes built-in salting, making it far more secure for password storage.

faqs.q: Can I reverse a hash back to the original text?
faqs.a: No. Hash functions are one-way by design. You cannot mathematically reverse a hash. Attackers use brute-force or rainbow tables to find inputs that match a hash, which is why strong passwords and salting are essential.

howToUseSteps: Enter or paste your text in the input field
Click 'Generate Hashes' to compute all hash values
Toggle 'Uppercase' for uppercase hex output
Copy any hash value with the copy button

uuid-generator.seoContent: UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) v4 generates random 128-bit identifiers. With 122 random bits, the probability of a collision is astronomically low. UUIDs are commonly used as database primary keys, session tokens, and distributed system identifiers.

faqs.q: What is a UUID?
faqs.a: UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit number used to uniquely identify information. Version 4 UUIDs are randomly generated, making collision probability astronomically low.

faqs.q: Are UUIDs truly unique?
faqs.a: While not mathematically guaranteed, UUID v4 has 2^122 possible values. The probability of generating a duplicate is essentially zero for practical purposes.

faqs.q: When should I use UUIDs?
faqs.a: Use UUIDs as database primary keys, API resource identifiers, session tokens, or any time you need a unique identifier without a central authority.

timestamp-converter.seoContent: A Unix timestamp represents the number of seconds since January 1, 1970 (UTC). It's widely used in programming, databases, and APIs. This tool auto-detects whether the input is in seconds or milliseconds.

faqs.q: What is a Unix timestamp?
faqs.a: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch). It's a universal way to represent time in computing.

faqs.q: What's the difference between seconds and milliseconds?
faqs.a: Unix timestamps in seconds are 10 digits (e.g., 1700000000), while milliseconds are 13 digits (e.g., 1700000000000). JavaScript uses milliseconds, most systems use seconds.

faqs.q: Does this tool handle timezones?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool shows both UTC and your local timezone when converting timestamps, so you can see the exact time in both.

faqs.q: What is a JWT?
faqs.a: JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe token format used for authentication and information exchange. It contains a header, payload, and signature.

faqs.q: Is it safe to decode JWTs here?

faqs.q: Why do programmers use hexadecimal?

faqs.q: What's binary used for?

cron-parser.seoContent: Cron is a time-based job scheduler in Unix-like systems. A cron expression consists of 5 fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week. Special characters include * (any), / (step), , (list), and - (range). Our online cron expression parser lets you validate and decode any cron schedule instantly. Common cron expressions include */5 * * * * (every 5 minutes), 0 0 * * * (daily at midnight), and 0 9 * * 1 (every Monday at 9am). Use this cron schedule generator for CI/CD pipelines, crontab debugging, automated backups, and recurring task planning.

faqs.q: What is a cron expression?
faqs.a: A cron expression is a string of 5 fields (minute, hour, day, month, weekday) that defines a schedule for recurring tasks in Unix-like systems.

faqs.q: What do the special characters mean?
faqs.a: * means any value, / means step (*/5 = every 5), , means list (1,3,5), - means range (1-5), and specific numbers mean exact values.

faqs.q: Can I see when my cron job will run next?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your cron expression and the tool will show the next scheduled execution times, plus a human-readable description.

faqs.q: What are the 5 fields in a cron expression?
faqs.a: The 5 fields are: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), and day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). Each field can use numbers, wildcards (*), ranges (-), lists (,), and steps (/).

faqs.q: What is the difference between cron and crontab?
faqs.a: Cron is the daemon (background service) that runs scheduled tasks. Crontab (cron table) is the file where you define your cron jobs and their schedules. You edit the crontab using the 'crontab -e' command.

faqs.q: What are common cron expressions for everyday tasks?
faqs.a: Every 5 minutes: */5 * * * *. Daily at midnight: 0 0 * * *. Every Monday at 9am: 0 9 * * 1. Every hour: 0 * * * *. First day of every month: 0 0 1 * *. Weekdays at 8am: 0 8 * * 1-5.

faqs.q: How does cron handle timezones?
faqs.a: Standard Unix cron uses the system's local timezone. There is no timezone field in a cron expression. To run jobs in a specific timezone, set the TZ variable in your crontab or use tools that support timezone-aware scheduling.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Spring cron and Unix cron?
faqs.a: Spring cron expressions have 6 fields (adding seconds as the first field), while Unix cron has 5 fields. Spring cron also uses different syntax for day-of-week (1-7 where 1=Monday) compared to Unix (0-6 where 0=Sunday).

faqs.q: What does a 502 Bad Gateway error mean?

mime-types.seoContent: MIME types (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) define the nature and format of a document or file. Web servers use MIME types in Content-Type headers to tell browsers how to handle files. Getting the MIME type wrong can cause browsers to download files instead of displaying them, or break file uploads. This tool lets you look up the correct MIME type for any file extension, or find which extensions correspond to a given content type. It includes hundreds of MIME types covering images, audio, video, documents, fonts, and application-specific formats.

faqs.q: What is a MIME type?
faqs.a: A MIME type is a string like 'text/html' or 'image/png' that tells the browser or client how to interpret and display a file. It consists of a type and subtype separated by a slash.

faqs.q: How do I find the MIME type for a file extension?
faqs.a: Type the file extension (e.g., .pdf, .webp) into the search box. The tool will show the corresponding MIME type and category.

faqs.q: What MIME type should I use for JSON?
faqs.a: Use 'application/json' for JSON data. For JSON with a specific schema, you can use vendor types like 'application/vnd.api+json'.

howToUseSteps: Enter a file extension (e.g., .svg) or MIME type (e.g., image/svg+xml)
Browse the results showing matching types and extensions
Click on any result to see full details
Copy the MIME type string for use in your code
useCases: Setting correct Content-Type headers in web servers
Building file type detection in applications

escape-unescape.name: Escape / Unescape
escape-unescape.description: 对 HTML、JavaScript 和 JSON 进行转义或反转义
escape-unescape.pageDescription: 为 HTML、JavaScript 或 JSON 转义特殊字符。免费使用，无需注册。
escape-unescape.seoContent: Character escaping converts special characters into safe representations to prevent injection attacks and parsing errors. HTML escaping converts characters like < > & into entities (< > &). JavaScript escaping handles quotes and backslashes in strings. JSON escaping ensures strings are valid within JSON documents. This tool supports all three escaping modes and their reverse operations. It is essential for security-conscious developers who need to sanitize user input, build safe HTML output, or debug encoded strings in logs and API responses.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HTML and JavaScript escaping?
faqs.a: HTML escaping converts < > & " to HTML entities for safe display in web pages. JavaScript escaping adds backslashes before quotes, newlines, and special characters for safe use in JS strings.

faqs.q: Why do I need to escape strings?
faqs.a: Unescaped strings can cause XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks in HTML, syntax errors in JavaScript, or invalid JSON. Escaping ensures special characters are treated as data, not code.

faqs.q: Can I unescape encoded strings back to plain text?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to Unescape mode and paste the encoded string. The tool will convert escape sequences back to their original characters.

howToUseSteps: Select the escaping format: HTML, JavaScript, or JSON
Choose Escape or Unescape mode
Paste your text into the input area
Copy the escaped or unescaped result

Preparing strings for JSON API payloads
Debugging escaped characters in log files

ip-calculator.name: IP 子网计算器
ip-calculator.description: 计算子网掩码、网络和广播地址
ip-calculator.pageDescription: 计算子网掩码、网络地址和广播地址。免费使用，无需注册。
ip-calculator.seoContent: IP subnetting divides a network into smaller subnetworks to improve performance and security. Understanding subnets is critical for network administrators, DevOps engineers, and anyone configuring cloud infrastructure. This calculator takes an IP address with a CIDR prefix (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) and instantly computes the subnet mask, network address, broadcast address, first and last usable host, and total number of hosts. It supports both IPv4 addresses and various CIDR notations from /8 to /30. All calculations are done locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What is CIDR notation?
faqs.a: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation like /24 indicates how many bits are used for the network portion of an IP address. /24 means 24 network bits and 8 host bits, allowing 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the number of hosts in a subnet?
faqs.a: The formula is 2^(32-prefix) - 2 for IPv4. The subtraction accounts for the network address and broadcast address. A /24 subnet has 2^8 - 2 = 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: What is the difference between network and broadcast address?
faqs.a: The network address is the first address in a subnet (all host bits 0) and identifies the subnet. The broadcast address is the last (all host bits 1) and sends packets to all hosts in the subnet.

howToUseSteps: Enter an IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
Enter the CIDR prefix length (e.g., /24) or subnet mask
View the calculated network address, broadcast, and host range
Copy any value you need for your network configuration
useCases: Planning IP address allocation for cloud VPCs
Configuring firewall rules with correct subnet ranges
Studying for network certification exams (CCNA, CompTIA)

fake-data.pageDescription: 生成假姓名、邮箱和地址，用于测试。免费使用，无需注册。

Using real personal data for testing creates privacy risks and compliance issues with regulations like GDPR. This tool generates fake but realistic names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, and other data types. All data is generated randomly in your browser using established patterns — no real personal information is used. You can generate single records or bulk data sets, and copy the results in various formats for use in your applications.

faqs.q: Is the generated data based on real people?
faqs.a: No. All names, emails, addresses, and phone numbers are randomly generated using common patterns and formats. No real personal information is used.

faqs.q: Can I generate data in bulk?
faqs.a: Yes. Specify the number of records you want to generate and the tool will create them all at once. You can copy the results as JSON or CSV.

faqs.q: What data types are supported?
faqs.a: Names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, companies, dates, UUIDs, IP addresses, and more. Each type produces realistic-looking values.

hmac-generator.name: HMAC 生成器
hmac-generator.pageDescription: 使用 SHA-256 或 SHA-1 生成 HMAC 签名。免费使用，无需注册。
hmac-generator.seoContent: HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) combines a cryptographic hash function with a secret key to verify both data integrity and authenticity. Unlike simple hashing, HMAC requires the secret key to generate and verify signatures, making it resistant to tampering. HMAC-SHA256 is the most commonly used variant and is required by many APIs and webhook systems (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify). This tool generates HMAC signatures using SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512 algorithms. Enter your message and secret key, and get the signature in hexadecimal or Base64 format. All computation happens locally.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HMAC and a regular hash?
faqs.a: A regular hash (like SHA-256) only takes a message as input. HMAC also requires a secret key, so only parties who know the key can generate or verify the signature. This prevents tampering.

faqs.q: Which HMAC algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: HMAC-SHA256 is the most common and recommended choice. It offers strong security and is required by most modern APIs. Use SHA-1 only for legacy compatibility.

faqs.q: How do I verify a webhook signature with HMAC?
faqs.a: Compute the HMAC of the webhook payload using your secret key, then compare it to the signature in the webhook header. If they match, the webhook is authentic and untampered.

howToUseSteps: Enter or paste the message to sign
Enter the secret key
Select the hash algorithm (SHA-256, SHA-1, or SHA-512)
Copy the generated HMAC signature in hex or Base64
useCases: Verifying webhook signatures from payment providers
Generating message authentication codes for secure communication

url-parser.name: URL 解析器
url-parser.description: 将 URL 解析为组件
url-parser.pageDescription: 将 URL 解析为协议、host、pathname 和参数。免费使用，无需注册。
url-parser.seoContent: URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) contain multiple components: protocol (https), hostname, port, pathname, query parameters, and fragment hash. Understanding URL structure is essential for web development, API design, and debugging network requests. This tool breaks any URL into its individual components for easy inspection. It decodes percent-encoded characters, parses query strings into key-value pairs, and validates URL format. Useful for debugging redirect chains, analyzing tracking parameters, and understanding complex API endpoints.

faqs.q: What are the parts of a URL?
faqs.a: A URL consists of: protocol (https://), hostname (example.com), port (:8080), pathname (/api/users), query string (?id=123&sort=name), and fragment hash (#section).

faqs.q: How are query parameters parsed?
faqs.a: Query parameters start after the ? character and are separated by &. Each parameter is a key=value pair. Values may be percent-encoded for special characters.

faqs.q: Does it handle encoded URLs?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool automatically decodes percent-encoded characters (like %20 for spaces) and displays the decoded values alongside the raw encoded form.

howToUseSteps: Paste a complete URL into the input field

Copy any component value you need

Validating URL format before using in applications

binary-text.seoContent: Binary representation is the foundation of all digital computing. Every character you see on screen is stored as a sequence of 0s and 1s. This tool converts text to its binary representation and back. Each character is converted to its UTF-8 binary encoding, displayed as 8-bit groups. It supports all Unicode characters including emoji and characters from non-Latin scripts. The tool is useful for learning about character encoding, debugging encoding issues, and understanding how computers store text data at the lowest level.

faqs.q: How does text to binary conversion work?
faqs.a: Each character is converted to its Unicode code point, then encoded as binary digits. ASCII characters use 8 bits (1 byte), while other Unicode characters may use 16 or 32 bits.

faqs.q: What encoding does this tool use?
faqs.a: The tool uses UTF-8 encoding by default, which is backward-compatible with ASCII and supports all Unicode characters.

faqs.q: Can I convert binary back to text?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to Binary → Text mode and paste your binary string (space-separated 8-bit groups). The tool will decode it back to readable text.

howToUseSteps: Select the conversion direction: Text → Binary or Binary → Text
Enter your text or binary string in the input area

Debugging encoding issues in text processing
Creating binary art or encoded messages
Understanding how computers store and process text

pem-decoder.name: PEM / 证书解码器
pem-decoder.pageDescription: 解码 PEM 格式的证书。免费使用，无需注册。
pem-decoder.seoContent: PEM (Privacy Enhanced Mail) is the most common format for SSL/TLS certificates, private keys, and certificate chains. PEM files are Base64-encoded with header and footer lines like -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----. This tool decodes PEM-formatted certificates and displays all X.509 fields: subject, issuer, validity dates, serial number, signature algorithm, public key details, and extensions like Subject Alternative Names (SANs). It is essential for DevOps engineers managing SSL certificates, debugging TLS handshake failures, and verifying certificate chains.

faqs.q: What information can I see from a PEM certificate?
faqs.a: You can see the subject (domain name), issuer (CA), validity dates, serial number, signature algorithm, public key type and size, and extensions like SANs and key usage.

faqs.q: Is it safe to paste my certificate here?
faqs.a: Yes. All decoding happens locally in your browser. Your certificate data is never sent to any server. Note: never paste private keys in any online tool.

faqs.q: What is the difference between PEM and DER format?
faqs.a: PEM is Base64-encoded text with header/footer lines, readable in any text editor. DER is the raw binary format. This tool only handles PEM format.

howToUseSteps: Paste your PEM-formatted certificate (including BEGIN/END lines)
View the decoded certificate details instantly
Check the validity dates, subject, and issuer information
Verify Subject Alternative Names (SANs) for your domains
useCases: Verifying SSL certificate details before installation
Debugging TLS handshake and certificate chain issues
Inspecting certificate SANs for multi-domain coverage

It automatically generates thead with header rows and tbody with data rows, applies optional CSS classes for styling, and produces valid HTML5 markup. You can customize the table with classes for popular CSS frameworks like Bootstrap or Tailwind. The generated markup is ready to copy and paste into your web project, documentation, or email templates.

faqs.a: You can paste CSV data (comma-separated values) or JSON arrays of objects. The first row of CSV or the object keys become table headers.

faqs.q: Can I customize the table styling?
faqs.a: Yes. You can add CSS classes to the table element (e.g., Bootstrap's 'table table-striped' or custom classes). The generated HTML uses semantic thead/tbody elements.

faqs.q: Does it generate responsive tables?
faqs.a: The tool generates standard HTML table markup. For responsiveness, wrap the output in a div with overflow-x: auto or use your CSS framework's responsive table classes.

bcrypt-generator.name: Bcrypt Hash 生成器
bcrypt-generator.description: 生成可配置成本的 bcrypt hash
bcrypt-generator.pageDescription: 生成可配置成本因子的 bcrypt 密码 hash。免费使用，无需注册。
bcrypt-generator.seoContent: Bcrypt is a password hashing function designed to be slow and computationally expensive, making brute-force attacks impractical. Unlike fast hashes like MD5 or SHA-256, bcrypt incorporates a configurable cost factor that controls how many iterations are performed. Each increase in cost doubles the computation time. Bcrypt also automatically generates and embeds a random salt, preventing rainbow table attacks. This tool generates bcrypt hashes from passwords with your chosen cost factor (typically 10-12 for web applications). It can also verify if a password matches a given bcrypt hash. All processing happens locally.

faqs.q: What cost factor should I use for bcrypt?
faqs.a: A cost of 10-12 is recommended for most web applications, balancing security and performance. Cost 10 takes about 100ms per hash. Each increment doubles the time.

faqs.q: Is bcrypt better than SHA-256 for passwords?
faqs.a: Yes. SHA-256 is designed to be fast, which makes it vulnerable to brute-force attacks. Bcrypt is intentionally slow and includes a built-in salt, making it much more secure for password storage.

faqs.q: Can I verify a password against a bcrypt hash?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter the password and the bcrypt hash, and the tool will tell you if they match. The salt is embedded in the hash, so no separate salt is needed.

howToUseSteps: Enter the password you want to hash
Set the cost factor (default: 10)
Click Generate to create the bcrypt hash
Copy the hash for use in your application's database
useCases: Generating password hashes for user registration systems
Testing bcrypt implementations in your application
Comparing different cost factors for performance tuning

faqs.q: 什么是 Go Struct？
faqs.a: Go 中的 Struct 是一种复合数据类型，它将变量组合在一起。与映射不同，Struct 提供类型安全性。

faqs.q: 'PascalCase' 字段命名是什么意思？
faqs.a: PascalCase 是 Go 导出结构体字段的命名约定。该工具会自动将 snake_case 和 kebab-case 转换为 PascalCase。

faqs.q: JSON 结构体标签有什么用途？
faqs.a: JSON 标签（例如 `json:"field_name"`）告诉 Go 的 encoding/json 包如何在 JSON 键和结构体字段之间进行映射。

faqs.q: 何时应使用 omitempty？
faqs.a: 对可选字段使用 omitempty。它告诉 Go 在字段具有零值时从 JSON 输出中省略该字段。

svg-to-jsx.name: SVG 转 JSX/React
svg-to-jsx.description: 将 SVG 标记转换为 JSX React 组件
svg-to-jsx.pageTitle: SVG 转 JSX/React 转换器
svg-to-jsx.pageDescription: 在线将 SVG 转换为 JSX React 组件。将 SVG 属性转换为驼峰命名，可包装为 React 组件。免费即时转换。
svg-to-jsx.seoContent: 在 React 中使用 SVG 图标和图形需要将 SVG 属性转换为 JSX 兼容语法。SVG 使用短横线命名属性如 stroke-width、fill-opacity 和 clip-path，在 JSX 中必须变为驼峰命名：strokeWidth、fillOpacity、clipPath。本工具自动处理所有这些转换。它还可以将 SVG 包装在带有导出语句的 React 组件中。非常适合将设计工具中的 SVG 转换为可复用的 React 图标组件。

faqs.q: 哪些 SVG 属性会被转换？
faqs.a: 所有短横线命名的 SVG 属性都转为驼峰命名：stroke-width → strokeWidth，fill-opacity → fillOpacity，clip-path → clipPath 等 40 多个属性。

faqs.q: 可以将 SVG 包装为 React 组件吗？
faqs.a: 可以。启用“包装为组件”选项即可生成带有 export 的完整 React 组件。您可以自定义组件名称。

faqs.q: 为什么在 React 中要移除 xmlns？
faqs.a: xmlns 属性仅在独立 SVG 文件中需要。在 JSX/React 中不需要，因为 SVG 嵌入在 HTML 中。移除它使代码更简洁。

faqs.q: 是否处理内联样式？
faqs.a: 是的。内联样式字符串转换为带有驼峰命名属性的 JavaScript 样式对象。

howToUseSteps: 将 SVG 标记粘贴到输入面板
设置组件名称并切换包装选项
点击转换生成 JSX 兼容的 SVG
将结果复制到 React 组件文件中

构建可复用 React SVG 组件的图标库
将静态 HTML 中的 SVG 资源迁移到 React
优化 React 渲染的内联 SVG

css-to-tailwind.name: CSS 转 Tailwind
css-to-tailwind.description: 将 CSS 样式转换为 Tailwind CSS 工具类
css-to-tailwind.pageTitle: CSS 转 Tailwind 转换器
css-to-tailwind.pageDescription: 在线将 CSS 转换为 Tailwind CSS 工具类。映射常见 CSS 属性到 Tailwind 类。免费迁移工具。
css-to-tailwind.seoContent: Tailwind CSS 是一个工具优先的 CSS 框架，使用预定义类替代自定义 CSS。从传统 CSS 迁移到 Tailwind 涉及将 CSS 属性映射到等效的工具类。本工具自动转换常见 CSS 属性，包括 display、position、flexbox、grid、间距、排版、颜色、边框等。对于没有精确 Tailwind 等效项的属性，它使用 Tailwind 的方括号表示法生成任意值类。转换器处理单个声明和带选择器的完整 CSS 规则集。

faqs.q: 所有 CSS 都能转换为 Tailwind 吗？
faqs.a: 不是所有 CSS 都有直接的 Tailwind 等效项。工具转换常见属性如 display、flexbox、排版和间距。复杂或不常见的 CSS 会标记为“未转换”以便手动处理。

faqs.q: 如何处理自定义颜色？
faqs.a: 自定义颜色使用 Tailwind 的任意值语法转换：color: #ff5733 变为 text-[#ff5733]。

faqs.q: 支持响应式断点吗？
faqs.a: 工具转换每个规则中的 CSS 属性。响应式类（sm:、md:、lg:）需要根据媒体查询断点手动添加。

faqs.q: 可以粘贴带选择器的 CSS 吗？
faqs.a: 可以。工具解析带选择器的 CSS 规则集并显示每个选择器的 Tailwind 类。也可以粘贴不带选择器的原始声明。

点击转换生成 Tailwind 类

将 Tailwind 类复制到 HTML 元素中

typescript-to-javascript.name: TypeScript 转 JavaScript
typescript-to-javascript.description: 将 TypeScript 代码编译为纯 JavaScript
typescript-to-javascript.pageTitle: TypeScript 转 JavaScript 转换器
typescript-to-javascript.pageDescription: 在线将 TypeScript 转换为 JavaScript。去除类型注解、接口和 TS 特定语法。免费即时转换。
typescript-to-javascript.seoContent: TypeScript 是 JavaScript 的类型超集，可编译为纯 JS。有时您需要快速去除 TypeScript 特定语法以获得干净的 JavaScript——用于与非 TS 项目共享代码、调试或学习 TypeScript 编译结果。本工具移除类型注解、接口、类型别名、泛型参数、访问修饰符（public、private、protected、readonly）、类型断言（as Type）、非空断言（!）和 declare 语句。它保留所有运行时 JavaScript 代码。所有处理都在浏览器中完成。

faqs.q: 哪些 TypeScript 语法会被移除？
faqs.a: 类型注解（: string）、接口、类型别名、泛型参数（<T>）、访问修饰符（public/private/protected/readonly）、类型断言（as Type）、非空断言（!）和 declare 语句。

faqs.q: 是否处理枚举？
faqs.a: 基本枚举会保留，因为它们有运行时 JavaScript 输出。const 枚举和环境枚举会被移除。

faqs.q: 输出可以用于生产环境吗？
faqs.a: 输出移除 TypeScript 语法以生成有效的 JavaScript。对于生产构建，建议使用官方 TypeScript 编译器（tsc）或 esbuild 等打包工具。

faqs.q: 是否降级现代 JavaScript 特性？
faqs.a: 不会。本工具仅去除 TypeScript 特定语法。现代 JS 特性（async/await、可选链等）保持不变。

howToUseSteps: 将 TypeScript 代码粘贴到输入面板
点击转换以去除 TypeScript 语法
检查干净的 JavaScript 输出
复制并在 JavaScript 项目中使用

学习 TypeScript 的编译结果

为文档转换 TypeScript 代码片段

json-to-graphql.name: JSON to GraphQL
json-to-graphql.description: Convert JSON data to GraphQL schema definitions
json-to-graphql.pageDescription: Convert JSON to GraphQL type definitions online. Generate accurate GraphQL schemas from JSON data with nested types and arrays. Free and instant.
json-to-graphql.seoContent: GraphQL uses a strongly-typed schema to define the shape of data available through an API. When designing a GraphQL API, you often start with sample JSON data from an existing REST endpoint or database. This tool analyzes your JSON structure and generates the corresponding GraphQL type definitions. It maps JavaScript types to GraphQL scalars (String, Int, Float, Boolean), creates separate type blocks for nested objects, and handles arrays as list types. The generated schema can serve as a starting point for your GraphQL server implementation. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How does JSON to GraphQL conversion work?
faqs.a: The tool analyzes your JSON structure and maps each field to the appropriate GraphQL type. Strings become String, numbers become Int or Float, booleans become Boolean, nested objects become separate types, and arrays become list types.

faqs.q: Does it generate a complete GraphQL schema?
faqs.a: It generates type definitions that you can use in your schema. You may need to add custom resolvers, mutations, and input types depending on your API design.

faqs.q: How are nested objects handled?
faqs.a: Nested objects are extracted into separate named types. For example, a user with an address object will generate both a User type and an Address type.

faqs.q: Is the output ready to use in a GraphQL server?
faqs.a: The generated types are valid GraphQL SDL (Schema Definition Language) and can be used directly in servers like Apollo, Yoga, or any SDL-first GraphQL framework.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root type name (default: Root)
Click Convert to generate GraphQL types
Copy the schema into your GraphQL server
useCases: Designing GraphQL schemas from existing REST API responses
Prototyping GraphQL types from sample data
Generating type definitions for GraphQL code generators

json-to-java.name: JSON to Java Class
json-to-java.description: Convert JSON data to Java class definitions
json-to-java.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Java POJO classes online. Generate Java classes with getters, setters, and Lombok support. Free, fast, and private.
json-to-java.seoContent: Java's strong type system requires defining classes before deserializing JSON data. Manually writing Java POJOs (Plain Old Java Objects) for complex JSON APIs is tedious and error-prone. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates complete Java class definitions with proper field types, constructors, getters, and setters. It supports Lombok's @Data annotation to reduce boilerplate. Nested objects become separate classes, arrays become List<Type>, and null values are handled with nullable types. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Java classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON data, set a root class name, and click Convert. The tool generates Java POJO classes with proper types, fields, constructors, getters, and setters.

faqs.q: What is the Lombok option?
faqs.a: When enabled, the tool adds Lombok's @Data annotation which auto-generates getters, setters, toString, equals, and hashCode methods, significantly reducing boilerplate code.

faqs.q: How are arrays handled?
faqs.a: JSON arrays are converted to List<Type> with appropriate generic types. The tool adds the java.util.List import automatically.

faqs.q: Can I use the generated classes directly?
faqs.a: Yes. The output is valid Java code ready to use with Jackson, Gson, or any JSON library. Just copy into .java files.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root class name (default: Root)
Toggle Lombok support if desired
Copy the generated Java classes into your project
useCases: Creating Java POJOs from REST API responses
Generating model classes for Spring Boot applications
Building typed data models for Android apps
Quickly scaffolding Java classes from sample data

json-to-kotlin.name: JSON to Kotlin
json-to-kotlin.description: Convert JSON data to Kotlin data classes
json-to-kotlin.pageTitle: JSON to Kotlin Data Class Converter
json-to-kotlin.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Kotlin data classes online. Generate idiomatic Kotlin code with nullable types and proper type inference. Free and instant.
json-to-kotlin.seoContent: Kotlin data classes provide a concise way to define typed data models. When working with JSON APIs in Kotlin (especially on Android), you need data classes that match the JSON structure. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates idiomatic Kotlin data classes with proper type inference. It handles nullable types for null values, uses List<Type> for arrays, and creates separate data classes for nested objects. The generated code works seamlessly with Kotlinx.serialization, Moshi, or Gson. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Kotlin data classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON, set the root class name, and click Convert. The tool generates Kotlin data classes with proper types for each field.

faqs.q: How are nullable types handled?
faqs.a: Fields with null values are typed as nullable (String?). You can also enable the nullable option to make all fields nullable.

faqs.q: Does it work with Android development?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated data classes are compatible with Retrofit, Moshi, Gson, and Kotlinx.serialization commonly used in Android apps.

faqs.q: How are nested objects converted?
faqs.a: Nested JSON objects become separate Kotlin data classes. For example, an address field generates both a Root data class and an Address data class.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root class name (default: Root)
Toggle nullable option if needed
Copy the generated Kotlin data classes into your project
useCases: Creating Kotlin data classes for Android API integration
Generating models for Ktor server applications
Building typed models for Kotlin Multiplatform projects
Converting API response samples to Kotlin types

json-to-csharp.name: JSON to C#
json-to-csharp.description: Convert JSON data to C# class definitions
json-to-csharp.pageDescription: Convert JSON to C# classes online. Generate C# class definitions with proper types and optional namespace. Free, fast, and private.
json-to-csharp.seoContent: C#'s strong type system is central to .NET development. faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to C# classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON data, set a root class name, optionally add a namespace, and click Convert. The tool generates C# classes with proper property types.

faqs.q: Does it work with System.Text.Json?

markdown-to-html.name: Markdown to HTML
markdown-to-html.description: Convert Markdown text to HTML markup
markdown-to-html.pageDescription: Convert Markdown to HTML online. Supports headers, bold, italic, code blocks, links, images, lists, and blockquotes. Free and instant.
markdown-to-html.seoContent: Markdown is a lightweight markup language widely used for documentation, README files, and content creation. Converting Markdown to HTML is essential for rendering content in web pages, email templates, and CMS systems. This tool converts Markdown syntax to clean HTML markup, supporting headers (h1-h6), bold and italic text, inline code and fenced code blocks, links, images, ordered and unordered lists, blockquotes, and horizontal rules. The output is clean, semantic HTML ready for use in any web project. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What Markdown syntax is supported?
faqs.a: Headers (#), bold (**), italic (*), code (`), code blocks (```), links, images, unordered lists (-), ordered lists (1.), blockquotes (>), and horizontal rules (---).

faqs.q: Does it support GitHub Flavored Markdown?
faqs.a: The tool supports common Markdown syntax including fenced code blocks with language hints. Some GFM extensions like tables and task lists are not yet supported.

faqs.q: Is the HTML output semantic?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool generates proper semantic HTML tags: h1-h6 for headings, strong for bold, em for italic, ul/ol for lists, blockquote for quotes, and pre/code for code blocks.

faqs.q: Can I use the output in email templates?
faqs.a: The generated HTML uses standard tags that work in email clients. You may want to add inline CSS for consistent email rendering.

Click Convert to generate HTML
Review the HTML output

Building HTML email bodies from Markdown drafts

html-to-markdown.name: HTML to Markdown
html-to-markdown.description: Convert HTML markup to Markdown text
html-to-markdown.pageDescription: Convert HTML to Markdown online. Transform HTML tags to Markdown syntax including headers, links, images, lists, and code blocks. Free and instant.
html-to-markdown.seoContent: Converting HTML to Markdown is useful when migrating content from web pages to Markdown-based systems like GitHub, Notion, or static site generators. This tool transforms HTML tags into equivalent Markdown syntax: h1-h6 become # headers, strong/b become **bold**, a tags become [links](url), img tags become ![images](src), lists become - or 1. items, and code blocks become fenced ```blocks```. It also decodes common HTML entities and cleans up excess whitespace. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What HTML tags are converted?
faqs.a: The tool converts h1-h6, strong/b, em/i, a (links), img (images), ul/ol/li (lists), blockquote, pre/code (code blocks), hr, p, and br tags.

faqs.q: Does it handle HTML entities?
faqs.a: Yes. Common entities like &, <, >, ", ', and   are decoded to their text equivalents.

faqs.q: What happens to unsupported tags?
faqs.a: Unsupported HTML tags are stripped, preserving their inner text content. The tool aims to extract readable Markdown from any HTML.

faqs.q: Can I convert a full web page?
faqs.a: You can paste any HTML snippet. For full pages, paste the body content. The tool handles most common HTML patterns found in articles and documentation.

Click Convert to generate Markdown
Review the Markdown output

Converting HTML documentation to Markdown for GitHub

toml-yaml.name: TOML to YAML / YAML to TOML
toml-yaml.description: Convert between TOML and YAML configuration formats
toml-yaml.pageDescription: Convert between TOML and YAML formats online. Bidirectional conversion for configuration files. Free, fast, and works in your browser.
toml-yaml.seoContent: TOML and YAML are popular configuration file formats used in modern development. TOML (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language) is used by Rust's Cargo, Python's pyproject.toml, and Hugo. YAML is used by Docker Compose, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, and many CI/CD tools. Converting between these formats is common when migrating projects or adapting configurations. This tool provides bidirectional conversion: TOML to YAML and YAML to TOML. It handles sections, nested tables, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What TOML features are supported?
faqs.a: The tool supports key-value pairs, sections ([section]), nested sections, arrays, inline tables, strings (quoted and bare), numbers, and booleans.

faqs.q: What YAML features are supported?
faqs.a: The tool supports key-value pairs, nested keys (indentation-based), arrays (- items and inline []), strings, numbers, booleans, and null values.

faqs.q: Can I convert in both directions?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the direction selector to switch between TOML → YAML and YAML → TOML conversion.

faqs.q: Does it preserve comments?
faqs.a: Comments are not preserved during conversion, as TOML and YAML have different comment syntaxes. Only data values are converted.

howToUseSteps: Select the conversion direction (TOML→YAML or YAML→TOML)
Paste your configuration data into the input panel
Click Convert to transform the format
Copy the converted output for use in your project

Migrating Docker Compose YAML to TOML format
Adapting pyproject.toml configurations for YAML-based tools
Comparing configuration formats for new projects

json-to-zod.name: JSON to Zod Schema
json-to-zod.description: Convert JSON data to Zod validation schemas
json-to-zod.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Zod validation schemas online. Generate type-safe Zod schemas from JSON data. Free, fast, and works in your browser.
json-to-zod.seoContent: Zod is a TypeScript-first schema validation library that lets you define schemas and validate data at runtime. When building TypeScript applications, Zod schemas provide both runtime validation and compile-time type inference. This tool analyzes your JSON data and generates corresponding Zod schemas with proper type mappings: strings become z.string(), numbers become z.number(), booleans become z.boolean(), arrays become z.array(), and nested objects become z.object(). The generated schemas can be used directly in your TypeScript project for form validation, API response validation, and more. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What is Zod?
faqs.a: Zod is a TypeScript-first schema declaration and validation library. It lets you define the shape of data and validates it at runtime while providing automatic TypeScript type inference.

faqs.q: How does JSON to Zod conversion work?
faqs.a: The tool analyzes your JSON structure and maps each value to the appropriate Zod schema method: z.string(), z.number(), z.boolean(), z.array(), z.object(), and z.null().

faqs.q: Can I use the output directly in my project?

faqs.q: Does it handle nested objects?

json-to-json-schema.description: Generate JSON Schema from JSON data

json-to-json-schema.seoTitle: About JSON to JSON Schema Conversion
json-to-json-schema.seoContent: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for annotating and validating JSON documents. It's widely used for API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger), form generation, configuration validation, and data interchange. This tool analyzes your JSON data and generates a JSON Schema (draft-07) that describes its structure. It correctly identifies types, marks all existing fields as required, handles arrays with item schemas, and creates nested schemas for objects. The output can be used with any JSON Schema validator or integrated into OpenAPI specifications. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: What JSON Schema draft is used?
faqs.a: The tool generates schemas following JSON Schema draft-07, which is widely supported by validators and tools.

faqs.q: Are all fields marked as required?
faqs.a: Yes. Since the tool infers the schema from sample data, all present fields are marked as required. You can adjust this manually after generation.

faqs.q: Does it handle nested objects?
faqs.a: Yes. Nested objects generate nested schema definitions with their own properties and required arrays.

faqs.q: Can I use this with OpenAPI/Swagger?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated JSON Schema is compatible with OpenAPI specifications. You can paste the schema into your API documentation.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the schema title
Click Convert to generate the JSON Schema
Copy the schema for use with validators or API docs

Generating validation schemas for REST APIs
Documenting data structures for team collaboration

css-to-js.name: CSS to JS Object
css-to-js.description: Convert CSS styles to JavaScript style objects
css-to-js.pageDescription: Convert CSS to JavaScript style objects online. Transform CSS properties to camelCase JS objects for React and CSS-in-JS. Free and instant.
css-to-js.seoContent: CSS-in-JS is a popular approach in modern frontend development, especially with React. Libraries like styled-components, Emotion, and React's inline styles use JavaScript objects instead of CSS strings. Converting CSS to JS objects requires changing property names from kebab-case to camelCase (font-size becomes fontSize), wrapping string values in quotes, and converting pixel values to numbers where appropriate. This tool automates the conversion process, handling selectors, property names, and values. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How are CSS property names converted?
faqs.a: Kebab-case CSS properties are converted to camelCase: font-size becomes fontSize, background-color becomes backgroundColor, border-radius becomes borderRadius.

faqs.q: Are pixel values converted to numbers?
faqs.a: Yes. Pure pixel values like 16px become the number 16. Values with other units (em, rem, %) remain as strings.

faqs.q: Does it handle CSS selectors?
faqs.a: Yes. CSS rules with selectors are converted to named JavaScript objects. Class selectors like .container produce a const named container.

faqs.q: Can I use the output with React?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated objects work with React's style prop, styled-components, Emotion, and other CSS-in-JS libraries.

howToUseSteps: Paste your CSS code into the input panel
Click Convert to generate JS objects
Review the camelCase property names
Copy the objects into your JavaScript/React project
useCases: Converting CSS to React inline style objects
Generating style objects for React Native
Converting design tool CSS output to JavaScript

graphql-to-typescript.pageDescription: Convert GraphQL schema to TypeScript types online. Generate TypeScript interfaces from GraphQL type definitions. Free and instant.
graphql-to-typescript.seoContent: GraphQL schemas define the shape of data in your API using SDL (Schema Definition Language). When building TypeScript clients or servers, you need TypeScript types that match your GraphQL schema for type safety. This tool converts GraphQL type definitions to TypeScript interfaces. It handles scalar types (String, Int, Float, Boolean, ID), object types, input types, enums, unions, and list types. Non-null types (!) become required fields, while nullable types become optional. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What GraphQL types are supported?
faqs.a: The tool supports type, input, enum, scalar, and union definitions. It handles both nullable and non-null (!) types, and list types ([Type]).

faqs.q: How are GraphQL scalars mapped?
faqs.a: String and ID become string, Int and Float become number, Boolean becomes boolean. Custom scalars default to unknown.

faqs.q: Does it handle enums?
faqs.a: Yes. GraphQL enums are converted to TypeScript enum declarations with string values matching the GraphQL enum values.

faqs.q: How is nullability handled?
faqs.a: Non-null types (!) become required TypeScript fields. Nullable types (without !) become optional fields with the ? suffix.

howToUseSteps: Paste your GraphQL schema (SDL) into the input

Copy the types into your TypeScript project

json-to-rust.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Rust structs with serde derive macros online. Generate typed Rust structs from JSON data. Free, fast, and private.
json-to-rust.seoContent: Rust's type system requires defining structs before deserializing JSON data with serde. Manually writing Rust structs for complex JSON APIs is time-consuming. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates Rust struct definitions with proper types (String, i64, f64, bool, Vec<T>), serde derive macros (Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone), and automatic snake_case field naming with #[serde(rename)] attributes when needed. Nested objects become separate named structs, and null values are wrapped in Option<T>. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Rust structs?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON, set the root struct name, select derive macros, and click Convert. The tool generates Rust structs with proper types and serde attributes.

faqs.q: What derive macros are available?
faqs.a: You can toggle Debug, Clone, Serialize, and Deserialize. The serde import is added automatically when Serialize or Deserialize is selected.

faqs.q: How are field names handled?
faqs.a: Field names are converted to snake_case. If the original JSON key differs, a #[serde(rename = "originalKey")] attribute is added.

faqs.q: How are null values handled?
faqs.a: Fields with null values are typed as Option<String>. This allows the field to be None when the value is null in JSON.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root struct name and derive options
Click Convert to generate Rust structs
Copy the structs into your Rust project

Building typed models for Actix-web or Axum servers
Generating serde-compatible types from JSON configs
Quickly scaffolding Rust data models from sample data

xml-to-json.name: XML to JSON
xml-to-json.description: Convert XML markup to JSON format
xml-to-json.pageDescription: Convert XML to JSON online. Transform XML documents to JSON with attribute handling, nested elements, and array detection. Free and instant.
xml-to-json.seoContent: XML and JSON are two of the most common data interchange formats. While XML uses tags and attributes, JSON uses key-value pairs and arrays. Converting XML to JSON is useful when migrating legacy systems, consuming SOAP APIs, or processing XML feeds in modern JavaScript applications. This tool parses XML and converts it to a structured JSON representation where elements become objects, attributes are prefixed with @, text content is stored as #text, and repeated elements automatically become arrays. It handles CDATA sections, self-closing tags, and nested structures. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How are XML attributes handled?
faqs.a: Attributes are prefixed with @ in the JSON output. For example, <item id="1"> becomes {"@id": "1"}.

faqs.q: How is text content represented?
faqs.a: Text content within elements is stored as #text. If an element has both attributes and text, both are preserved: {"@attr": "val", "#text": "content"}.

faqs.q: Does it handle repeated elements?
faqs.a: Yes. When multiple sibling elements share the same tag name, they are automatically grouped into a JSON array.

faqs.q: Does it support CDATA sections?
faqs.a: Yes. CDATA sections are parsed and their content is included as text in the JSON output.

Click Convert to generate JSON

Copy the JSON for use in your application

Migrating XML configuration files to JSON format
Processing RSS/Atom feeds as JSON data
Transforming XML exports from legacy systems

favicon-generator.seoContent: A favicon is the small icon displayed in browser tabs, bookmarks, and history. This favicon generator creates ICO and PNG favicons from text or emoji with customizable colors, sizes, and border radius. Generate minimal valid ICO files in standard sizes: 16x16 for browser tabs, 32x32 for taskbar icons, and 48x48 for Windows shortcuts. You can also create 180x180 Apple Touch icons for iOS. Download as ICO, PNG, or copy as a Base64 data URI for inline HTML embedding. Supports custom background colors, font sizes, and rounded corners for modern favicon designs.

faqs.q: What favicon sizes do I need?
faqs.a: Common: 16x16 (tab), 32x32 (taskbar), 48x48 (Windows), 180x180 (Apple Touch).

faqs.q: What format for favicons?
faqs.a: PNG is widely supported. ICO can contain multiple sizes.

faqs.q: Can I use emoji?
faqs.a: Yes! Modern browsers support emoji favicons with custom backgrounds.

faqs.q: What is the minimal valid ICO file format?
faqs.a: A minimal valid ICO file contains a 6-byte header (magic bytes, type, image count), a 16-byte directory entry (size, color info, data offset), and the image data. The smallest practical favicon is a 16x16 pixel ICO file, typically a few hundred bytes.

faqs.q: Should I use ICO, PNG, or SVG for my favicon?
faqs.a: ICO is the traditional format that supports multiple sizes in one file. PNG is widely supported and simpler. SVG favicons are the newest option, supported in modern browsers, and scale perfectly to any size. Use ICO for maximum compatibility.

faqs.q: How do I add a favicon to my website using Base64?
faqs.a: Add this to your HTML <head>: <link rel="icon" href="data:image/png;base64,...">. This embeds the favicon directly in your HTML without needing a separate file. This tool generates the Base64 data URI ready to use.

faqs.q: What favicon sizes should I include for PWA manifest?
faqs.a: For Progressive Web Apps, include 192x192 and 512x512 PNG icons in your manifest.json. Also include 16x16, 32x32, and 180x180 (Apple Touch) for complete browser and device coverage.

faqs.q: Why isn't my favicon showing up?
faqs.a: Common issues: browser cache (try hard refresh with Ctrl+Shift+R), wrong file path in the <link> tag, incorrect MIME type, or the ICO file is malformed. Place favicon.ico in your site root as a fallback, since browsers check there by default.

cron-expression-generator.faq4a: 可以。使用逗号分隔值（例如，0 9,17 * * * 在每天上午9点和下午5点运行）。使用连字符表示范围（例如，1-5 表示周一到周五）。
cron-expression-generator.faq5a: Cron 默认使用系统本地时区。某些系统允许指定 TZ 变量或使用 UTC。请查看您的系统文档。

faqs.q: What is a Base64 data URI for images?
faqs.a: A data URI embeds image data directly in HTML or CSS using the format data:image/png;base64,... This eliminates an extra HTTP request but increases HTML size by ~33%. Best for small icons under 10KB.

faqs.q: Should I use Base64 images in production?

faqs.q: Is it safe to decode JWT tokens in an online tool?
faqs.a: Yes, when the tool processes data entirely in your browser. DevToolBox never sends your JWT to any server — all decoding happens client-side using JavaScript.

faqs.q: What information is inside a JWT token?
faqs.a: A JWT contains three parts: the header (algorithm and type), the payload (claims like user ID, roles, expiration), and the signature (verification hash). The header and payload are Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted.

faqs.q: Can I verify a JWT signature online?
faqs.a: You can decode and inspect JWT tokens without the secret key. However, signature verification requires the signing key (for HMAC) or public key (for RSA/ECDSA), which should never be shared in online tools.

faqs.q: Why does my JWT show as expired?
faqs.a: The 'exp' claim in the payload is a Unix timestamp. If the current time exceeds this value, the token is expired. Check the decoded expiration date and compare it with the current UTC time.

faqs.q: How do I use capture groups in regex?
faqs.a: Wrap parts of your pattern in parentheses to create capture groups. Use (?:...) for non-capturing groups and (?<name>...) for named groups. The tester shows each group's match separately.

faqs.q: What does the g, i, m flag mean in regex?
faqs.a: g (global) finds all matches, i (case-insensitive) ignores letter case, m (multiline) makes ^ and $ match line starts/ends instead of string starts/ends. s (dotAll) makes . match newlines.

faqs.q: Why is my regex not matching?
faqs.a: Common issues: forgetting to escape special characters (. * + ? etc.), missing flags (especially g for multiple matches), or using syntax from a different regex flavor. Try simplifying your pattern and testing piece by piece.

faqs.q: What are HTML entities?
faqs.a: HTML entities are special codes that represent characters which have special meaning in HTML (like < > & ") or characters that cannot be typed on a standard keyboard. They start with & and end with ; (e.g., & for &, < for <).

faqs.q: Why do I need to encode HTML entities?
faqs.a: Encoding prevents XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks and ensures special characters display correctly. Without encoding, characters like < and > are interpreted as HTML tags, potentially breaking your page or creating security vulnerabilities.

faqs.q: What is the difference between named and numeric entities?
faqs.a: Named entities use descriptive names (e.g., & < ©). Numeric entities use character codes (e.g., & < ©). Named entities are more readable but not all characters have names. Numeric entities work for any Unicode character.

faqs.q: When should I use HTML entities vs UTF-8?
faqs.a: With UTF-8 encoding (recommended for all modern websites), you only need to encode &, <, >, and " in HTML context. Special characters like accented letters can be typed directly. Use entities only for these 4 HTML-special characters and for invisible characters.

faqs.a: Beautifying adds whitespace and indentation for readability (development). Minifying removes all whitespace for smaller file sizes (production). Both preserve the exact same styling behavior.

faqs.q: What are HTTP headers?
faqs.a: HTTP headers are metadata sent between client and server with every request and response. They control caching (Cache-Control), security (Content-Security-Policy), content type (Content-Type), authentication (Authorization), and more.

faqs.q: How do I check HTTP headers for a website?

faqs.q: How does IP address lookup work?
faqs.a: IP lookup queries geolocation databases that map IP address ranges to physical locations. These databases are compiled from ISP registrations, routing data, and other sources. Accuracy varies: country is 95-99% accurate, city is 50-80% accurate.

faqs.q: Is IP geolocation always accurate?
faqs.a: No. IP geolocation is approximate. It is accurate for country (95-99%) but less so for city (50-80%). VPN users, mobile networks, and corporate proxies can show incorrect locations. Never rely on IP location for critical decisions.

faqs.q: Can I find someone's exact address from their IP?
faqs.a: No. IP addresses do not reveal exact addresses. At best, you can determine the city or region. Only the Internet Service Provider (ISP) can map an IP to a specific subscriber, and they only share this with law enforcement via legal process.

faqs.q: What information can I get from an IP address?
faqs.a: Approximate geographic location (country, region, city), ISP name, organization name, timezone, AS number, and whether it is a known VPN/proxy/Tor exit node. You cannot get personal information like name or street address.

faqs.q: What is color blindness simulation?
faqs.a: Color blindness simulation shows how your design appears to people with different types of color vision deficiency. It helps identify problematic color combinations where important distinctions may be invisible to colorblind users.

faqs.q: How many people are color blind?
faqs.a: Approximately 8% of men and 0.5% of women have some form of color vision deficiency. The most common type is red-green color blindness (deuteranopia/protanopia), affecting about 6% of men. This means roughly 1 in 12 male users.

faqs.q: How do I design for colorblind users?
faqs.a: Never rely solely on color to convey information. Use patterns, labels, icons, or underlines alongside color. Ensure sufficient contrast ratios (WCAG AA: 4.5:1). Test with simulation tools. Avoid problematic pairs like red/green or blue/purple.

faqs.q: What are the types of color blindness?
faqs.a: Protanopia (no red cones), deuteranopia (no green cones), tritanopia (no blue cones), and achromatopsia (total color blindness). Red-green deficiency (protanopia + deuteranopia) is by far the most common, affecting ~6% of males.

faqs.q: How do I read a cron expression?
faqs.a: A cron expression has 5 fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), day of week (0-7). For example, '30 9 * * 1-5' means 'At 9:30 AM, Monday through Friday'.

faqs.q: What does */5 mean in cron?
faqs.a: The */5 syntax means 'every 5th unit'. In the minute field, */5 means every 5 minutes (0, 5, 10, 15...). In the hour field, */2 means every 2 hours. It is called a step value.

faqs.q: What is the difference between * and ? in cron?
faqs.a: The asterisk (*) means 'every value'. The question mark (?) is used in some cron implementations (like Quartz) for day-of-month or day-of-week to mean 'no specific value'. Standard cron uses * for both.

faqs.q: How do I schedule a job for the first Monday of every month?
faqs.a: Standard cron cannot directly express this. Use '0 0 1-7 * 1' (runs on Monday when the date is 1-7) or implement the logic in your script to check if today is the first Monday.

faqs.q: What is a SAML assertion and how do I decode it?
faqs.a: A SAML assertion is an XML document issued by an identity provider (IdP) that contains authentication and authorization statements about a user. Assertions are Base64-encoded for transport. Paste the encoded string into this tool to instantly decode it to readable XML.

faqs.q: How do I decode a SAML response from my browser?
faqs.a: Open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the Network tab, and look for the POST request to your SP's ACS URL. The SAMLResponse parameter in the form data is the Base64-encoded response. Copy and paste it into this tool.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SAML and OAuth?
faqs.a: SAML is an XML-based protocol primarily used for enterprise SSO between identity providers and service providers. OAuth 2.0 is a JSON-based authorization framework used for API access and third-party app authorization. SAML handles authentication while OAuth focuses on authorization.

faqs.q: Can this tool decode Base64-encoded SAML with Deflate compression?
faqs.a: Yes. SAML Requests typically use Base64 + Deflate compression (as per the HTTP-Redirect binding). This tool automatically detects and handles both plain Base64 and Base64+Deflate encoded SAML data.

faqs.q: Is it safe to paste SAML tokens into this decoder?
faqs.a: Yes, completely safe. All decoding happens locally in your browser. Your SAML data is never sent to any server, stored, or logged. The tool runs entirely client-side.

faqs.q: What information is contained in a SAML response?
faqs.a: A SAML response typically contains: the issuer (IdP), a digital signature, status codes, one or more assertions with the subject (NameID), authentication statements, attribute statements (like email, name, roles), and conditions (audience restriction, validity period).

faqs.q: Why is my SAML response failing to decode?
faqs.a: Common causes include: incomplete copy of the Base64 string, URL-encoded characters that need to be decoded first, or the data is not actually SAML. Make sure you copy the entire SAMLResponse value without truncation.

faqs.q: What is XPath and how does it work?
faqs.a: XPath (XML Path Language) is a query language for selecting nodes from XML documents. It uses path-like expressions to navigate the XML tree structure. For example, //book selects all book elements, and //book[@price>30] selects books with a price attribute greater than 30.

faqs.q: What is the difference between XPath and CSS selectors?
faqs.a: XPath can navigate both forward and backward in the XML/HTML tree and supports complex conditions, while CSS selectors only navigate downward. XPath is more powerful for XML querying, while CSS selectors are simpler and faster for HTML styling. XPath supports text content matching; CSS selectors do not.

faqs.q: How do I select elements by attribute in XPath?
faqs.a: Use the @ symbol to select attributes. For example: //div[@class='main'] selects div elements with class 'main', //input[@type='text'] selects text inputs, and //*[@id='header'] selects any element with id 'header'.

faqs.q: What is the difference between / and // in XPath?
faqs.a: A single slash (/) selects from the root or current node's direct children only. Double slash (//) selects matching nodes anywhere in the document regardless of depth. For example, /bookstore/book selects direct children, while //book selects all book elements at any level.

faqs.q: Can I use XPath to query HTML documents?
faqs.a: Yes. XPath works on both XML and well-formed HTML (XHTML). Most browsers support XPath queries via document.evaluate(). This tool accepts any valid XML input, including XHTML documents.

faqs.q: How do I test XPath expressions for Selenium?
faqs.a: Paste your page's HTML source into the XML Input field, then test your XPath locator expressions. This helps you validate selectors before using them in Selenium's find_element(By.XPATH, '...') or Playwright's page.locator('xpath=...') calls.

faqs.q: What XPath functions are supported?
faqs.a: This tool supports standard XPath 1.0 functions including: text(), contains(), starts-with(), string-length(), count(), sum(), position(), last(), not(), and boolean operators (and, or). These work for filtering and matching nodes.

faqs.q: What are Protocol Buffers (protobuf)?
faqs.a: Protocol Buffers is a language-neutral, platform-neutral binary serialization format developed by Google. It's used to serialize structured data for communication between services, data storage, and more. Protobuf is more compact and faster than JSON or XML.

faqs.q: Can I decode protobuf without a .proto schema file?
faqs.a: Yes. This tool performs schema-less decoding by parsing the raw wire format. It identifies field numbers and wire types, and attempts to interpret values as integers, strings, or nested messages. However, without a schema, field names and exact types are unknown.

faqs.q: What is the difference between protobuf and JSON?
faqs.a: Protobuf is a binary format that is smaller (3-10x) and faster to parse than JSON. JSON is human-readable and self-describing. Protobuf requires a schema (.proto file) for proper encoding/decoding, while JSON is schema-optional. Protobuf is preferred for high-performance inter-service communication.

faqs.q: How is protobuf used in gRPC?
faqs.a: gRPC uses protobuf as its default serialization format. Service interfaces and message types are defined in .proto files, which generate client and server code. When gRPC sends data over the network, messages are serialized to protobuf binary format.

faqs.q: What are protobuf wire types?
faqs.a: Protobuf uses wire types to indicate how values are encoded: Varint (0) for integers, 64-bit (1) for fixed64/double, Length-delimited (2) for strings/bytes/nested messages, and 32-bit (5) for fixed32/float. The wire type is encoded alongside the field number in the binary data.

faqs.q: How do I get protobuf data from network traffic?
faqs.a: Use tools like Wireshark, Charles Proxy, or browser DevTools to capture gRPC or HTTP/2 traffic. Extract the protobuf payload bytes and paste them as hex into this decoder. For gRPC-Web traffic, the payload is often Base64-encoded.

faqs.q: Is protobuf binary data safe to paste into this tool?
faqs.a: Yes. All decoding is performed locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server. Your protobuf payloads remain private and are never stored or logged.

faqs.q: What are tokens in AI language models?
faqs.a: Tokens are the basic units that LLMs use to process text. A token can be a word, part of a word, or a punctuation mark. In English, one token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words. For example, 'chatbot' is one token, while 'understanding' might be split into 'under' + 'standing'.

faqs.q: How many tokens can GPT-4 and Claude handle?
faqs.a: GPT-4o supports up to 128K tokens context window. Claude 3.5 Sonnet supports 200K tokens. GPT-4 Turbo supports 128K tokens. These limits include both input (prompt) and output (response) tokens combined.

faqs.q: How are AI API costs calculated based on tokens?
faqs.a: AI APIs charge per token, usually priced per 1 million tokens. Input tokens (your prompt) and output tokens (the response) are priced differently, with output tokens typically costing 3-5x more. This tool shows both input and output costs for each model.

faqs.q: Is the token count exact for all models?
faqs.a: The count is an approximation based on the average of ~4 characters per token for English text. Each model uses its own tokenizer (GPT uses tiktoken, Claude uses its own BPE tokenizer), so exact counts may vary slightly. The estimate is accurate enough for cost planning.

faqs.q: How can I reduce token usage to lower API costs?
faqs.a: Remove unnecessary whitespace and verbose instructions. Use concise prompts. Avoid repeating context. Use system messages efficiently. Consider shorter model responses by setting max_tokens. For large documents, use chunking or summarization before sending to the API.

faqs.q: Do different languages use different amounts of tokens?
faqs.a: Yes. English is the most token-efficient language for most LLMs. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and other non-Latin languages typically require 2-3x more tokens per word because the tokenizers were primarily trained on English text. This significantly affects API costs for non-English use.

faqs.q: What is a context window in AI models?
faqs.a: The context window is the maximum number of tokens an AI model can process in a single request, including both the input prompt and the generated output. If your text exceeds the context window, it will be truncated or the API will return an error.

faqs.q: Does this tool send my text to any AI service?
faqs.a: No. Token counting is performed entirely in your browser using a local approximation algorithm. Your text is never sent to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any other service.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SCSS and CSS nesting?
faqs.a: Native CSS nesting requires the & symbol for element selectors (e.g., & span {}), while SCSS allows implicit nesting. The converter handles this difference automatically.

faqs.q: What is Base64 encoding used for?
faqs.a: Base64 encoding converts binary data to ASCII text, making it safe to transmit over text-based protocols like HTTP and email.

faqs.q: Does encoding make data secure?
faqs.a: No. Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Anyone can decode it. For security, use encryption tools.

faqs.q: Why does encoded data look longer?
faqs.a: Base64 encoding increases data size by about 33% because it represents 3 bytes of binary data as 4 ASCII characters.

faqs.q: What is TOML?
faqs.a: TOML (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language) is a configuration file format designed to be easy to read. It's used by Rust (Cargo.toml), Python (pyproject.toml), and many other tools.

faqs.q: Is TOML better than JSON for config files?
faqs.a: TOML is more human-readable with support for comments and cleaner syntax for nested structures. JSON is better for data interchange and API responses.

faqs.q: Does this tool handle nested TOML tables?
faqs.a: Yes. The converter supports sections [section], dotted keys, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans.

faqs.q: Is my data safe?
faqs.a: All conversion happens in your browser. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.q: What TOML features are supported?
faqs.a: Basic key-value pairs, sections (tables), arrays, strings (basic and literal), integers, floats, and booleans are supported.

toml-to-json.seoContent: TOML (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language) is a popular configuration file format used by Rust (Cargo.toml), Python (pyproject.toml), Hugo, and many developer tools. This free online TOML to JSON converter parses TOML files into structured JSON and converts JSON back to TOML format. All processing runs entirely in your browser for maximum privacy and speed.

faqs.q: What is an INI file?
faqs.a: INI (Initialization) files are simple text-based configuration files with sections in [brackets] and key=value pairs. They're used by PHP, MySQL, Windows, and many applications.

faqs.q: Does this handle INI sections?
faqs.a: Yes. Sections like [database] are converted to nested JSON objects. Keys outside any section become top-level properties.

faqs.q: Are comments preserved?
faqs.a: Comments (lines starting with ; or #) are ignored during parsing, as JSON doesn't support comments.

faqs.q: Does it handle data types?
faqs.a: Yes. The parser automatically detects numbers, booleans (true/false), and strings. Quoted values are treated as strings.

faqs.q: Is my data safe?
faqs.a: Absolutely. All parsing happens in your browser. No data is sent to any server.

ini-to-json.seoContent: INI (Initialization) files are one of the oldest and simplest configuration formats, widely used by PHP (php.ini), MySQL (my.cnf), Windows applications, and many legacy systems. This free online INI to JSON converter parses INI sections and key-value pairs into structured JSON, and can convert JSON back to INI format. Processing runs entirely in your browser.

faqs.q: What is a ULID?
faqs.a: A ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is a 26-character, 128-bit identifier that encodes a timestamp and random data. ULIDs sort naturally by creation time.

faqs.q: ULID vs UUID - which should I use?
faqs.a: Use ULID when you need time-sorted IDs (databases, logs). Use UUID when you need maximum compatibility. ULIDs are URL-safe and more compact than UUIDs.

faqs.q: Are ULIDs truly unique?
faqs.a: Yes. ULIDs combine a 48-bit millisecond timestamp with 80 bits of randomness, making collisions virtually impossible.

faqs.q: Can I extract the timestamp from a ULID?
faqs.a: Yes! The first 10 characters encode the creation timestamp. Use the decode section below the generator to extract it.

faqs.q: What encoding do ULIDs use?
faqs.a: ULIDs use Crockford's Base32 encoding (0-9, A-Z excluding I, L, O, U), which is URL-safe and case-insensitive.

ulid-generator.seoTitle: About ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier)
ulid-generator.seoContent: ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is a modern alternative to UUID that provides 128-bit unique identifiers with built-in timestamp sorting. Each ULID encodes a millisecond-precision timestamp in the first 48 bits and 80 bits of cryptographic randomness, formatted as a 26-character Crockford Base32 string. This makes ULIDs ideal for database primary keys, distributed systems, and any use case requiring chronologically sortable unique identifiers.

helm-chart-validator.seoContent: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes, using Charts to define, install, and manage K8s applications. This validator checks your Chart.yaml for required fields (apiVersion, name, version) and values.yaml for common configuration issues.

faqs.q: What Chart.yaml fields are required?
faqs.a: apiVersion (v2 recommended), name, and version are required. description, type, and appVersion are strongly recommended.

faqs.q: Does it validate templates?
faqs.a: This tool focuses on Chart.yaml and values.yaml validation. Template rendering requires helm template command locally.

faqs.q: What Helm version is supported?
faqs.a: Both Helm v2 (apiVersion: v1) and Helm v3+ (apiVersion: v2) chart formats are validated, with v2 recommended.

howToUseSteps: Paste your Chart.yaml on the left
Paste your values.yaml on the right
Review validation results for both files
Fix any errors before packaging the chart
useCases: Checking chart structure in CI/CD pipelines
